questions.question: Select the most defensible meaning of 'spill the beans':

options.text: To refuse to testify in court

questions.explanation: Rule RC-01 ke anusaar, 'spill the beans' ka universally established arth confidential ya secret jankari ko prematurely reveal kar dena hota hai.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate idiom:
"After twenty years of bitter family litigation over the ancestral haveli, the cousins decided to ________ and divide the property amicably."
questions.explanation: Rule RC-13 ke anusaar, 'twenty years of bitter litigation' ek purani dushmani ko darshata hai jise khatam karne ke liye 'bury the hatchet' lagta hai.

questions.question: "To draft the special leave petition before tomorrow morning's filing deadline, the advocate had to burn the midnight oil." This means he:

options.text: Lit kerosene lamps in his office

questions.explanation: 'Burn the midnight oil' ka arth der raat tak jaag kar mehnat se kaam karna hota hai.

questions.question: Which idiom describes completing an essential action at the very last possible moment just before disaster strikes?

options.text: At the drop of a hat

questions.explanation: 'In the nick of time' theek aakhri kshan par aakar disaster ya nuksan rokne ko darshata hai.

questions.question: Choose the antonymous behavior to 'lose one's temper':
questions.explanation: 'Lose one's temper' ka exact opposite 'keep one's cool' (shaant aur sanyamit rehna) hota hai. Options B, C, aur D anger se jude hain.

questions.question: "Setting up an enterprise data center for the high court will cost an arm and a leg." This means the data center will:
questions.explanation: 'Cost an arm and a leg' ka arth atyadhik mehanga hona (exorbitantly expensive) hota hai.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect sentence that distorts an established idiom:

options.text: He explained the ratio decidendi in a nutshell.
The senior clerk advised him to keep his nose to the grindstone.
The auditor was censured for turning the blind eyes to the audit objection.
We decided to call it a day after cataloging the files.

questions.explanation: Rule RC-04 ke anusaar, established idiom 'turn a blind eye' hota hai (singular 'eye' with indefinite article 'a'). '*Turning the blind eyes*' distorted and invalid hai.

questions.question: Which of the following actions best illustrates 'jumping the gun'?

options.text: Filing a writ petition after obtaining certified copies and thorough research
Issuing appointment letters to candidates before the selection board finalized the results
Working overtime during judicial inspection week
Revising a draft three times to ensure perfection

questions.explanation: 'Jump the gun' nirdharit samay ya official permission se pehle premature action lene ko kehte hain (Option B).

questions.question: Which expression is classified as a PROVERB rather than an IDIOM?

options.text: A penny saved is a penny earned

questions.explanation: Rule RC-06 ke mutabiq, 'A penny saved is a penny earned' ek complete standalone sentence hai jo traditional wisdom deta hai, isliye yeh Proverb hai.

questions.question: To perform an official duty 'by the book' means to:

options.text: Follow all prescribed rules and statutory procedures rigorously

questions.explanation: 'By the book' ka arth official statutory procedures aur rules ka aksharasah palan karna hota hai.

questions.question: Select the option that is the OPPOSITE in communicative intent to 'beat around the bush':
questions.explanation: 'Beat around the bush' (indirect evasion) ka direct communicative opposite 'call a spade a spade' (blunt truth) hota hai.

questions.question:
In the sentence: "The magistrate warned the accused that one must hold ________ tongue in court."
The correct pronoun to complete the sentence is:
questions.explanation: Rule RC-05 ke mutabiq, jab subject impersonal pronoun 'one' ho ('one must hold...'), toh possessive pronoun strictly 'one's' hota hai ('hold one's tongue').

questions.question: "A double-edged sword" refers to something that:

options.text: Is extremely sharp and dangerous to touch physically
Can have both favourable and adverse consequences
Has been manufactured using two metals
Is used exclusively by military personnel

questions.explanation: 'A double-edged sword' aisi sthiti ya decision ko kehte hain jisme fayda aur nuksan dono hone ki sambhavna hoti hai.

questions.question: If someone 'cannot see the forest for the trees', they are:

options.text: Lost in a dense woodland area
Unable to understand the broader situation because of excessive focus on minor details
Suffering from acute nighttime vision loss

questions.explanation: 'Not see the forest for the trees' ka matlab chhoti details mein itna ulajh jana hota hai ki main broad picture nazar na aaye.

questions.question: When a public servant who committed fraud is summoned by the vigilance bench to 'face the music', it means he must:

options.text: Sing in a ceremonial musical ensemble
Accept and confront the unpleasant punishment for his misconduct
Listen to sound recordings of the inquiry
Defend himself by accusing his subordinates

questions.explanation: 'Face the music' ka established arth apni galti ya apradh ka anjaam aur punishment jhelna hota hai.
